---
title: Forms
description: Configure create and edit forms with typed fields, validation, defaults and relations.
kind: how-to
metaTitle: Create and edit forms
---

Create and edit forms are generated from the table. Declare `create.fields` and `update.fields` to choose exactly what each form writes; the server rejects any other field.

A generated form follows the list's columns, a column's `secondary` line included: a column's `label` names its control, a `reference` column is a picker, and a column whose `format` is money, such as `{ kind: "money", minorUnits: 2 }` on `totalCents`, takes the amount in major units, `74.35`, and stores `7435`. A column the database needs a value for is marked required, a column with a plain default such as an enum's `draft` starts there, and the create form leaves out a record timestamp the database fills, such as `created_at default now()` or `updated_at`. A defaulted date the user sets, such as `due_on default current_date`, stays as an optional field.

## Declare the fields

```ts
resource(schema.users, {
  columns: ["email", "name", "role", "createdAt"],
  create: {
    fields: [
      { name: "email", type: "email", required: true },
      { name: "name", required: true },
      { name: "role", type: "select", options: ["member", "admin"] },
    ],
  },
  update: {
    fields: [
      { name: "name", required: true },
      { name: "role", type: "select", options: ["member", "admin"] },
    ],
  },
})
```

## Controls

`type` picks the input: text, textarea, number, money, email, password, url, date, datetime, time, boolean, switch, checkbox, select, multiselect, radio, json, markdown, tags, reference, hidden or color. Add `label`, `help` or `placeholder` when the name is not enough.

A `markdown` field edits plain text. The record page and the drawer show it formatted: headings, paragraphs, `-` lists, `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` `` and links to `https://`, `mailto:` or a path. HTML in the text stays text.

The server checks the value against the type wherever it comes from: the form, the JSON API, a CSV import or an action form. An `email` must be an address the browser's email input accepts, a `url` a full address that starts with `http://` or `https://`, such as `https://example.com`, a `color` a `#rrggbb` value, a `time` a time of day such as `09:30`, and a `number`, `date` or `datetime` field a number or a date. On an edit, a value the row already holds is kept.

`options` takes strings, `{ label, value }` pairs, or a function resolved on the server per request. A `select`, `multiselect` or `radio` field whose column has an `enumOf` format lists the enum's labels without `options`.

## Money fields

A `money` field edits an amount stored in minor units, such as cents, the way the `money` column format shows it:

```ts as="FieldDef<RowOf<'invoices'>>"
{ name: "amountCents", label: "Amount", type: "money", currency: "EUR" }
```

The form shows `399.99` with the currency's sign beside it, in the admin's decimal separator, and the server stores `39999`. `currency` defaults to `formatting.currency`, and `minorUnits`, the digits after the decimal point (0 to 8), to the currency's own: 2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD.

`storage` says what the column holds. `"minor"`, the default for an integer column, stores whole minor units. `"major"`, the default for a `numeric`, `decimal` or float column, stores the amount itself, `399.99`. Saving a form without touching a valid amount keeps the stored value exactly. A stored value the currency cannot hold, such as `1999.5` minor units, shows unrounded as `19.995`, and the form will not save until someone corrects it.

A comma works as the decimal separator. Text that is not an amount is rejected with `invalidMoney`, and an amount with more decimals than `minorUnits` with `moneyTooPrecise`. The JSON API takes and returns the column's own value. Pair a minor-unit field with `format: { kind: "money", minorUnits: 2 }` on the column, so the list and record show the same amount, and a range filter on that column takes the same amount.

## Relation fields

A reference field stores the foreign key and shows a searchable label from another resource:

```ts as="FieldDef<RowOf<'monitors'>>"
{
  name: "customerId",
  label: "Customer",
  reference: { resource: "customers", labelField: "email" },
  required: true,
}
```

The stored value is the target's primary key. The lookup applies the target resource's access and tenant scope.

## Validation and defaults

The resource schema, `required` and each field's `validate`, a Zod schema or a function returning a message, run in one round, so a submit shows every field's problem at once. A field the schema already refused keeps the schema's message and its `validate` does not run. `required` marks the control required and the server rejects a missing value. A NOT NULL column without `required` is checked too: a create that leaves it empty, or an edit that clears it, fails with its "is required" message.

A timestamp column gets a `datetime-local` control that shows the stored time on the admin's clock, `formatting.timeZone` (UTC when unset), and the server reads the posted time in that zone. Saving without touching it keeps the stored seconds. A `type: "date"` field shows the day.

`defaultValue` fills a key the submission left empty, on the server. On a visible field it also pre-fills the control, so the browser sees it. A create field without `defaultValue` starts on its column's literal database default, such as `draft` for `status text default 'draft'`, as a generated form does. Put trusted values such as the tenant on a `hidden: true` field, or in `create.defaultValues`, to keep them off the page. When both name a key the submission left empty, `create.defaultValues` wins. A fixed default of a `select`, `radio` or `multiselect` field must be one of its fixed `options`; `defineAdmin` refuses one that is not and names the options, since the form would start empty.

### Rejection messages

A rejected write returns one message per field, from `labels.form`. A missing value reads `required` (`"{label} is required"`). A value that is not its column's type reads `invalidNumber`, `invalidBoolean` or `invalidDate`; one that does not fit its field's `type` reads `invalidEmail`, `invalidUrl`, `invalidColor` or `invalidTime`; and a money amount reads `invalidMoney`, or `moneyTooPrecise` when it has too many decimals. A value the database refuses reads `taken` (`"{label} is already taken"`) for a unique column and `missingReference` for a foreign key. A value outside a select's choices or a schema enum reads `invalidOption`, whatever message the enum carries, so it is in the admin's language; see [database constraint violations](/docs/reference/errors#database-constraint-violations). Any other message is the one your schema or `validate` wrote: `z.string().min(3, "Pick a longer slug")` shows as written. The [language presets](/docs/reference/define-config#language-presets) translate the built-in ones, and `{label}` is the field's [one label](/docs/build/resources#field-labels).

## Restrict fields

`readOnly` and the resource's `fieldAccess` apply to rendering and to writes. The form shows a field the user may not write as read-only, leaves out one they may neither read nor write, and its route drops both from what it saves; an API or programmatic write that carries such a field is rejected. `readOnly` wins over `fieldAccess.write`. A `readOnly` or `hidden` function is called on the server with the stored row on edit, and on create with the values the form starts with: `create.defaultValues`, each field's `defaultValue`, then the column's database default. So `hidden: (row) => row.status === "draft"` hides the field on a new record whose status starts as `draft`. On an import row or a JSON create, `hidden` and `required` are judged on those values with the row's own on top, and a field is read-only when its `readOnly` is true for the starting values or for the row's, so a client cannot unlock a field by sending the value its predicate checks. It runs once per page, not as the user types. `hidden` only removes the control. See [Roles and permissions](/docs/guides/permissions).

## Submission

Forms post to FlowPanel's route handlers. A create returns to the list with the new row highlighted for two seconds and a "Customer created" toast (`labels.saving.created`); an update returns to the row with "Changes saved" (`labels.saving.saved`). The form sends one request at a time: a double click or Enter during a save does nothing, and the form stays locked until the next page opens.

A rejected submit keeps the button enabled; submitting again moves focus to the first field in error. Each error shows under its field, and the banner above the button appears only for an error no field on the form can show.

While a form has unsaved changes, leaving it asks first: reloading or closing the tab shows the browser's prompt, and Cancel or any link in the admin opens a "Discard unsaved changes?" dialog (`labels.saving`). For a multi-step transaction or several resources at once, build a custom page. Every option: [FieldDef](/docs/reference/resources#fielddef).
